solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Such a mammal's position on a trail regularly overlooked

parts.note: a place is a position

indicators.note: every other letter of these words is passed over, leaving the even-placed ones

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes where some animal sits on a path, though it keeps being missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly overlooked' drops O, A, R, I from 'on a trail', leaving NTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Placental is a word for mammals whose young are nourished in the womb by a placenta, as most mammals are.

clue.text: Apparently good place for orchestra and singer

parts.note: PI is short for pious, so outwardly good or sanctimonious
the orchestra pit sits below the front of a stage

explanation.surface: A venue seems ideal for both an orchestra and a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, crossword shorthand for pious, is goodness that may be only for show, hence 'Apparently'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit is a small songbird, and crosswords often call birds singers.

clue.text: State going into broadcasting? I'm cool with that

indicators.note: says the word for state is put inside the word for broadcasting

parts.note: airing a programme is broadcasting it
a condition is a state

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs, happy enough with a state of affairs being put on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the device itself speaking: it is what keeps a room cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Air conditioning is the system that cools a building, so it could say it is cool with that.

clue.text: Nostalgic feelings when head lost income

indicators.note: the first letter of the longings word is dropped

parts.note: yearnings are wistful longings, often for the past

explanation.surface: Someone pines for the past after losing their job and its pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money a person makes from work, their income.

clue.text: Double whiskey — canned?

indicators.note: to be canned is to be put in a can, that is a tin, so the letter goes inside one

parts.note: the question mark flags that canned is stretched to mean put in a tin, a can
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: At the bar someone asks whether a double measure of whisky comes in a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canned' means put in a tin: W inside TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin is an exact counterpart, a double of someone.

clue.text: Admired appearance due for revamp: read on!

parts.note: a look is an appearance

indicators.note: the word due is to be remade, its letters rearranged

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to carry on to the next page

explanation.surface: A makeover is overdue, and the reader is urged to keep reading about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To look up to someone is to respect and admire them, an idiom.

clue.text: In turn, doctor very brave just opening heart

indicators.note: the whole string is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: only the first letter of brave is used

explanation.surface: One after another, a medic and a very brave patient have open-heart surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosom is the chest, and figuratively the heart, seat of the emotions.

clue.text: Philosopher tours east, warning of danger

indicators.note: the philosopher goes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Francis Bacon was an English philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker travelling in the East sounds an alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon was a hilltop fire lit to signal danger, such as an approaching enemy.

clue.text: One gives a convict life, as an interim measure

definitions.meaning: a ... halts a death sentence, letting the condemned prisoner live
more widely, a ... is any temporary postponement

explanation.surface: A reprieve spares a prisoner, if only for now.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal sense is a suspended death sentence; the general sense is a temporary delay of something unwelcome.

clue.text: Office a Tory left, sacked after a month

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the month

parts.note: May is a month

indicators.note: something sacked is ransacked, thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician leaves a post, fired after only a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' rearranges A, TORY and L into ORALTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayoralty is the office of mayor, or the term it is held.

clue.text: James's version of the Mona Lisa?

definitions.text: James's version of the Mona Lisa?

parts.words: James's version of the Mona Lisa?
parts.note: Henry James wrote a novel with this title, and Leonardo's famous painting is literally a picture of a woman

explanation.surface: It asks how a painter called James would render Leonardo's masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'James' looks like a painter, but it is the novelist Henry James.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mona Lisa depicts a woman, and Henry James's 1881 novel bears that very description as its title.

clue.text: Family must follow as well understood

indicators.note: the family word is placed after the other

parts.note: too means as well
kin are family members

explanation.surface: Relatives are expected to follow and be well understood too.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something in is to grasp or comprehend it, an idiom.

clue.text: Love alluring woman no end: time for action?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring

indicators.note: the last letter of the woman word is dropped

parts.note: a houri is a beautiful nymph of Islamic paradise, hence any alluring woman

explanation.surface: A romance with a seductress that never ends makes one ask when to act.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero hour is the moment set for an operation, especially a military attack, to begin.

clue.text: Tool order Charlie has left for workers

indicators.note: the letter for Charlie departs and the workers take its place

parts.note: to instruct is to order
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A tool is ordered, but Charlie has gone off to the workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument is an implement or tool, especially a precise one.

clue.text: Time away from poor old American native

indicators.note: the time letter is taken out of the word for poor

parts.note: indigent means poor

explanation.surface: A long-absent, impoverished elderly man returns to his American homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigenous means originating in a place, as native people or plants do.

clue.text: In secret, observe landlord

indicators.note: says the observing word sits inside the secret word

parts.note: inner means private or hidden, as in inner thoughts
to keep a rule or festival is to observe it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a quiet eye on the man who owns the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub landlord runs an inn, so is an innkeeper.

clue.text: Ruthless chap avoiding pained expression

indicators.note: the cry of pain is left out of the chap word

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A merciless man feels no pain himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell is an old adjective meaning cruel or deadly, as in one fell swoop.

clue.text: Disguises trick with performing animals for audience

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle

indicators.note: says the animals word is to be heard by listeners, so only its sound counts

parts.note: seals are the classic performing animals of the circus

explanation.surface: A circus hides its scam behind an animal act staged for the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for audience' turns SEALS into the same-sounding CEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to hide it, as a disguise does.

clue.text: Group of countries taking part in a tournament

indicators.note: only part of the words is taken, a stretch of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A bloc of nations enters a sporting competition.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance of member states.

clue.text: Piece of data, a single line added to one paper

indicators.note: the line comes after the word for one, joined on to it

parts.note: a stat is a statistic, a piece of data
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as the word one
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: An office report adds a figure and a solitary line to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery is writing materials, chiefly paper and envelopes.

clue.text: One million after tax

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
post- is a prefix meaning after

explanation.surface: Someone is a millionaire only once the taxman has taken his share.
explanation.definitionFit: An impost is a duty or levy, a tax.

clue.text: Rodent leading with its tail, and not very big

indicators.note: the rodent's last letter goes to the very front

parts.note: nor means and not
a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: A mouse runs backwards, tail first, and is hardly a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: NOR then MOUSE gives NORMOUSE; 'leading with its tail' moves the final E to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means huge, of very great size.

clue.text: Grab fruit, two packs a penny

parts.note: a rugby scrum is formed when the two packs of forwards bind together
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A shopper grabs fruit, two packs for a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the forwards of each side are a pack. To scrump is British slang for stealing apples from an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumping is the schoolboy habit of pinching fruit, especially apples, from trees.

clue.text: Papers, one of them missing formerly

indicators.note: the former word is left out of the newspaper's name

parts.note: the Express is a British newspaper, one of the papers
ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: The newspapers report that one of their own has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express is a British national tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: The press means newspapers and journalists collectively.

clue.text: Copy of Henry Green taken round

indicators.note: the green word is wrapped around the letter

parts.note: eco- means environmentally friendly, green
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A copy of a novel by Henry Green is passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Green was an English novelist, which is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a repetition or imitation, a copy of an original.

clue.text: Problematic gift of cocaine polished off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are spoiled and reordered

explanation.surface: A troublesome present of cocaine was finished off in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polished off' looks like eating up the drug, but 'off' alone is the anagram signal for COCAINE POLISHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisoned chalice is an honour or job that looks attractive but brings trouble, an idiom.

clue.text: Alarm not starting properly

indicators.note: the first letter of the alarm word is dropped

parts.note: fright is alarm or sudden fear

explanation.surface: An alarm clock fails to go off properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Right as an adverb means correctly, as in do it right.

clue.text: You lovely beaches! So many?

parts.note: thou is the old form of you
sands are beaches, here praised as lovely

explanation.surface: A poet addresses glorious beaches, marvelling at how many there are.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousands means a great number, as many as the grains on a beach.
